newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rival Palestinian factions call for joint strike.
newsitem.headline: Rival Palestinian factions call for joint strike.

text.p: Rival Palestinian factions issued a joint statement on Wednesday calling for a Palestinian day of mourning and two-hour strikes across the West Bank and Gaza.

"(We call on) the Palestinian masses to go out and march in the city centres in all regions. The central march will take place in Ramallah at Manara Square at 1030 (0830 GMT) to take part in the funerals of the confronting martyrs who defend Arab Jerusalem," the leaflet said.
The statement, signed by eight Palestinian movements, was the first of its kind since rival Palestinian factions joined forces during the 1987-1993 Palestinian intifada or uprising.
The joint statement called on Palestinians to close schools and shops from 0800 GMT to 1000 GMT on Thursday in solidarity with those killed in Wednesday's clashes in the West Bank and Gaza.

Factions listed on the joint statement were Fatah, which backs Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's peace deals with Israel, the leftist Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP), the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) and the Islamic fundamentalist Hamas.
The leaflet came after at least four Palestinians were killed and hundreds wounded in the bloodiest clashes in the West Bank and Gaza since the 1994 introduction of Palestinian self-rule.
